               <ns0:p n="17">17. I have therefore whereof I may glory through Jesus Christ, in those things which per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tain to God <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> Having received this grace of Apostleship, and having had great success in my Labours, multitudes be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing converted by my Ministry, I have whereof to Glory, or I have matter of Glorying and Rejoycing. But then he adds, that this Glorying of his, was not in himself, but in and <ns0:hi>through Iesus Christ,</ns0:hi> by whose grace he did what he did, <ns0:hi>vid.</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 15.10. And also, that it was not in any thing that concerned himself, but in things per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />taining to God, which concerned his Worship and Service, and wherein his Ministry consisted. In the foregoing verse he described his Apostleship in termes, that were borrow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed from the <ns0:hi>Livitical</ns0:hi>-Priesthood; and here contriving the same metaphor, he calleth the execution of his Function, a performing of things pertaining to God, which is that for which the Priests of old were ordained, <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 5.1.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18. For I will not dare to speak of any of those things, which Christ hath not wrought by me, <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>towards the obedience of the</ns0:hi> Gentiles.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 1.5. & 16.26.</ns0:note> to make the Gentiles obedient <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> I dare not speak of more then is true, or of any thing that was not really done by me: Or, else the mean<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing is, I dare not speak of any thing that I have done of my self, I acknowledg, that what ever good hath come to the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> by my means, it was wrought by Christ whose Instrument I have only been, <ns0:hi>vid.</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 3.5.</ns0:note> by word and deed <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Some joyn these words to the obedience of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> by the preaching of the Gospel they were made obedi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ent in word and deed. But they are better joyned with the former words, Christ wrought in and by the Apostle <ns0:hi>Paul,</ns0:hi> both by word and deed. By word is understood his publick preaching, and private instruction; and by deed, the example of his good Works, or Godly Life: Or else by deed ye may understand the Miracles that he wrought, and the Labour and Travel that he underwent; of which in the following verse.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19. Through <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>the power of signs and wonders.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> mighty signs and wonders <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Or by the power of signes and wonders, which ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ved to confirm my Commission from God, and the truth of what I Preached, and so helped forward the obedi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ence and Conversion of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles, vid.</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 12.12. If there be any difference betwixt Signs and Wonders, 'tis only gradual. I find them often conjoyned in Scripture, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 24.24. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 4.48. <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 2.43. & 5.12. and 7.36. and 14.3.</ns0:note>, by the power of the spirit of God <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Which blessed the Words, Deeds and Miracles of the Apostle, and wrought effectually by them in the <ns0:hi>Gen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tiles.</ns0:hi> The word, <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, Power or Vertue is twice used in this verse; it is first applyed to Signs and Won<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ders, to shew their Efficacy; and then to the Spirit of God, to shew that he was the efficient cause of that Efficacy.</ns0:note>; so that from Jerusalem, and round about unto Illyri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cum <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">This sheweth the pains and travel of the Apostle, to bring the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> to the obedience of Faith. <ns0:hi>Illyricum</ns0:hi> is said to be in the utmost parts of <ns0:hi>Greece,</ns0:hi> bordering up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on the Sea, which is thereupon called <ns0:hi>Illyricum Mare.</ns0:hi> It is thought to the be Country now called <ns0:hi>Sclavo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="3 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>,</ns0:hi> and that is distant from <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> about 350 <ns0:hi>German</ns0:hi> Miles, which makes above a thousand <ns0:hi>English</ns0:hi> Miles; yet it seems he did not travel in a direct and strait line, but round about, or in a circle, as the word imports, fetching a circuit. Some Writers have given us out of the Acts, a particular History of his perigrination from <ns0:hi>Damascus,</ns0:hi> where he began his Ministry<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> he went into <ns0:hi>Arabia,</ns0:hi> and after three years returned to <ns0:hi>Damascus,</ns0:hi> and from thence to <ns0:hi>Ierusa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lem</ns0:hi>; from <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> he went to <ns0:hi>Caesarea,</ns0:hi> and so to <ns0:hi>Tar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sus</ns0:hi>; from <ns0:hi>Tarsus Barnabas</ns0:hi> brought him to <ns0:hi>Antioch,</ns0:hi> and from thence to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> to carry relief to the <ns0:hi>Iewes:</ns0:hi> From <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> they returned to <ns0:hi>Antioch</ns0:hi>; from <ns0:hi>Antioch</ns0:hi> he and <ns0:hi>Barnabas</ns0:hi> went to <ns0:hi>Seleucia,</ns0:hi> then to <ns0:hi>Cyprus,</ns0:hi> and to some Cities of <ns0:hi>Pamphylia,</ns0:hi> and so to another <ns0:hi>Antioch</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Pisidia:</ns0:hi> From thence to <ns0:hi>Lycaonia,</ns0:hi> and then returned to <ns0:hi>Antioch</ns0:hi> From whence they had been recommended by the Church. From <ns0:hi>Antioch</ns0:hi> they were sent to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> about the question of the Circumcision, and returned to <ns0:hi>Antioch</ns0:hi> with the Apostles Decree. From thence he went through <ns0:hi>Syria</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ciliciae</ns0:hi> visiting the Churches. Then he went through <ns0:hi>Phrygia, Galatia</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mysia</ns0:hi>; then to <ns0:hi>Troas,</ns0:hi> where by a Vision he was called unto <ns0:hi>Macedonia,</ns0:hi> and so came into the parts of <ns0:hi>Europe:</ns0:hi> First to <ns0:hi>Phillippi</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Macedonia,</ns0:hi> then to <ns0:hi>Thessalonica</ns0:hi>; from thence to <ns0:hi>Athens,</ns0:hi> and then to <ns0:hi>Corinth</ns0:hi>; from thence to <ns0:hi>Ephesus:</ns0:hi> and going to visit the Churches of <ns0:hi>Galatia</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Phrygia,</ns0:hi> returned to <ns0:hi>Ephesus:</ns0:hi> From <ns0:hi>Ephesus</ns0:hi> he went again to <ns0:hi>Macedonia,</ns0:hi> from thence to <ns0:hi>Treas</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Miletions</ns0:hi>; and thence by <ns0:hi>Tyrus</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Caesarea,</ns0:hi> and other Cities, he came to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> where he was ta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken and put in bonds. Thus you have an account of the Apostles Travels which he abridgeth here, when he sayes, <ns0:hi>That it was from</ns0:hi> Jerusalem <ns0:hi>round about unto</ns0:hi> Illyricum.</ns0:note>, I have <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>fulfilled.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> fully preached the Gospel of Christ <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">i. e. <ns0:hi>I have filled all these Countries with the Gospel of Christ.</ns0:hi> The word signifieth to fulfil, <ns0:hi>vid. Col.</ns0:hi> 4.8. This he calleth the finishing his Ministry, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 20.24.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:432" />20. Yea, so have <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>such an ambition have I had.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> I strived to preach the Gospel, not where Christ was named, lest I should build upon another mans foundati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21. But, as it is written, To whom he was not spoken of, they shall see: and they that have not heard, shall understand <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">He gives a reason why he chose to preach the Gos<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pel in these places, because Christ had not been named or Preached there before; this he saith was his Ambiti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on, and a thing that he greatly coveted; he was unwil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ling to build upon another mans Foundation, to put his sickle into anothers harvest, to derive the Glory to himself, which would be due to others, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 10.15, 16. Again, another reason why he Preached the Gospel where Christ had not been named, was this, that so by him, as an Apostle of Christ, and in his Ministry, that the Scrip<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture might be fulfilled, which you have in <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 52.15. <ns0:hi>To whom he was not spoken of, they shall see,</ns0:hi> &c. See the Notes there.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22. For which cause also <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Thes. 2.17, 18.</ns0:note> I have been <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>many wayes.</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>often times.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> much hindred from coming to you <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Hitherto he hath excused his manner of Writing, now he makes an Apology for his not coming unto them. They at <ns0:hi>Rome</ns0:hi> might be ready to say, if he hath travel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led into so many Countries, Why could he not all this while give us a visit? To this he answers, it was not from any want of respect or good will to them, but for another cause which he had already assigned, and that was, the Preaching of Christ where he had not been na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />med; for this cause, he sayes, he had been much hindred; He looked upon that as the more necessary work, the planting of Churches is more then the watering of them. He told them, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 1.13. of his being hindred from com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing to them, and now he acquaints them more particu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />larly with the reason which he concealed before. The word (<ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>) rendred <ns0:hi>much,</ns0:hi> signifieth many; and it implies that he was many times hindred, and many wayes; but this was the chief.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23. But now having no more place in these <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>climates.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> parts, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 1.11. ver. 32.</ns0:note> having a great desire these ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny years to come unto you <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Having given the reason why he came not to them hitherto, in the following words he assures them, he would do it hereafter. And here he saith, He was the more enclined so to do. <ns0:hi>First,</ns0:hi> Because he had no more place in those parts. <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> As before in those places where Christ had not been named, or his Gospel Preach't, he had no new Churches there to be found, and he had ordained Elders in every City to build upon his Founda<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion. The word rendred <ns0:hi>parts,</ns0:hi> signifyes Climates. <ns0:hi>i. e,</ns0:hi> Pla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces which ly o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> divers Elevations of the Pole. And then <ns0:hi>Secondly,</ns0:hi> Because he had long longed so to do, he had de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sired it for many years, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 1.10, 11.</ns0:note>;</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24. Whensoever I take my journey into Spain, I will come to you: For I trust to see you in my journey <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Here he sets down the time when he would visit them. <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> When he took his Journey into <ns0:hi>Spain.</ns0:hi> He saith, he trusted he should see them then, he was not assured of it, he had no revelation from God concerning it, he he could make no absolute promise. See <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 28.</ns0:note>, and to be brought on my way thitherward by you <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> By some of you; this he did promise himself from them, and indeed it was usually done by the Churches he visited. <ns0:hi>vid. Act.</ns0:hi> 17.15. not that he affected any train or pomp, but it was done for his guidance and safety, as he travel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led through unknown and dangerous wayes.</ns0:note>, if first I be somwhat filled <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Gr. <ns0:hi>with you</ns0:hi> ver. 32.</ns0:note> with your <ns0:hi>company</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">This he adds, least they should think he meant to make no stay with them, he gives them to understand, that he did not intend to leave them, till they were mutually filled and satisfied with one anothers company and society.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25. But now <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Act. 19.21. and 24.17.</ns0:note> I go unto Jerusalem to mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nister unto the Saints <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Some might be ready to say, if <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> hath no more place in those parts where he is, and hath such a longing desire to see us, why then doth he not presently come to us? To this he answers, that for the present he could not come, because he had a weighty affair upon his hands, which was to go up to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> to Minister to the Saints. <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> To carry thither certain Collections and Contributions from the <ns0:hi>Gentile</ns0:hi> Churches for their relief. He useth a <ns0:hi>Participle</ns0:hi> of the pesent tense in the Original, to shew that this work is now in hand, and it would not stay or hold him long. Though indeed his work was to preach the Gospel, and not to serve Tables; yet it seems, likely that the Churches of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> who were moved by him to this Contribution, had committed the same to his care. 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 8.4.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26. For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 16.1, 2.</ns0:note> it hath pleased them of Macedo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nia and Achaia<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> to make a certain <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>commu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nication.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> contribu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion for the <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>the poor of the Saints.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> poor saints which are at Jeru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />salem <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">For the understanding of these words, you need only to read 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 8.1. and 9.2. When he saith, it <ns0:hi>hath pleased them,</ns0:hi> it is implyed, that it was not extorted or squeez'd out of them; but that it proceeded from a ready and willing mind, and that they took delight there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />in. The word here rendred <ns0:hi>Contribution,</ns0:hi> properly sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifieth Communication, which implyeth a mutual exchange, or entercourse between the givers and the receivers; the one Contributing Alms, the other Prayers and Intercessions to God. He speaks elsewhere of Communicating, con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerning <ns0:hi>Giving</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Receiving, Phil.</ns0:hi> 4.15.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27. It hath pleased them <ns0:hi>verily</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">He makes this repetition, as to commend the <ns0:hi>Greci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ans,</ns0:hi> so also to admonish the <ns0:hi>Romans</ns0:hi> to the like benevo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lence.</ns0:note>, and their debters they are <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> are Debtors to the <ns0:hi>Iewes</ns0:hi>; though what they sent them was a Gift, yet it was also a Debt, it was due by the Law of Charity, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 13.8. and by the Law of Gratitude and Equity, they had re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceived from them, and they were obliged in some sort to make returnes to them.</ns0:note>, For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 11.17.</ns0:note> if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 9.11. Gal. 6.6.</ns0:note> their duty is also, to minister to them in car<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nal things <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">By the Spiritual things of the <ns0:hi>Iewes,</ns0:hi> of which the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> were made partakers, you may understand all those things of which mention is made, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 9.4, 5. More particularly, the Gospel with the Ministry, and Ordinances thereof: The Gospel was first Preached to the <ns0:hi>Iewes,</ns0:hi> and from <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> it was spread abroad among the <ns0:hi>Gentiles, vid. Luke</ns0:hi> 24.47. <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 1.4, 8. By the carnal things of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> you may understand their Gold and Silver, with all things needful for the sustentation of the body: you have a parallel-place in 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 9.7.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28. When therefore I have performed this, and have sealed to them this fruit <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> After that I have dispatched this business<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and safely delivered the Almes of the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> Churches to the <ns0:hi>Iewes,</ns0:hi> wherewith I am intrusted, it is put into my hands as a Treasure sealed in a bag or che<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t, that it may not be diminished or imbezeled; he calls it Fruit, because it proceeded from their Faith and Love, and because it would abound to their account, <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 4.17. it would benefit them that received it, but much more them that gave it.</ns0:note>, I will come by you into Spain <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e. I will take you, or your City in my way thither,</ns0:hi> he told them as much before. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 24. This he really inten<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ded, but it is generally concluded, that he was prevented; that he never went this Journy into <ns0:hi>Spain.</ns0:hi> The purposes of men are ruled and over-ruled by the Providence of God, <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 16.9.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29. And I am sure that when I come unto you, I shall come in the fulness of the blessing of the Gospel of Christ <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> As some expound it, <ns0:hi>I shall find you furnished with all Spiritual and Gospel Blessings</ns0:hi>: This sence agrees with <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 14. But others rather think, that he speaks of what he should bring with him, and not of what he should find there. Therefore it may better be expounded by <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 1.11, 12. He assures himself he should impart unto them much Knowledg, Grace and Comfort; that he should enrich, and fill them with all the <ns0:hi>Blessings of the Gospel of Christ.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:432" />30. Now <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">In the Conclusion, he commends himself to their <ns0:hi>Prayers.</ns0:hi> This is usual with him, in his other Epistles, <ns0:hi>vid. Eph.</ns0:hi> 6.18. <ns0:hi>Col.</ns0:hi> 4.3. 2 <ns0:hi>Thes.</ns0:hi> 3.1. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 13.18.</ns0:note> I beseech you, brethren, for the Lord Jesus Christs sake <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> If not for my sake, yet for <ns0:hi>his sake,</ns0:hi> who is most dear to you.</ns0:note>, and for the love of the Spirit <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> If you <ns0:hi>love the Spirit of God:</ns0:hi> Or rather if the <ns0:hi>Grace of Love</ns0:hi> be wrought in you by the <ns0:hi>Spirit,</ns0:hi> shew it in this thing. This pathetical way of speaking is frequent with this Apostle, <ns0:hi>vid. chap.</ns0:hi> 12.1. <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 2.1.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 1.11.</ns0:note> that ye strive together with me in <ns0:hi>your</ns0:hi> prayers to God for me <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">That you <ns0:hi>strive,</ns0:hi> as those that be in an Agony; It is a Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />litary word: He bespeaks their earnest and importunate <ns0:hi>Prayers</ns0:hi> in his behalf. <ns0:hi>Iacob</ns0:hi> prayed after this manner, so did <ns0:hi>Elijah</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Epaphras, Col.</ns0:hi> 4.12. He <ns0:hi>Prayed</ns0:hi> himself, and he desired them to joyn with him, and help him; as <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Hur</ns0:hi> helped <ns0:hi>Moses.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31. That I may be delivered from them that <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>are diso<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>dient.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> do not believe in Judea, and that my ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vice which <ns0:hi>I have</ns0:hi> for Jerusalem, may be accep<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ted of the saints <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Here are two things more particularly, which he de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sireth them to Beg of God in his behalf. First, <ns0:hi>That he may be delivered from them that did not believe:</ns0:hi> Or were disobedient, and refractory in <ns0:hi>Iudea.</ns0:hi> He knew the <ns0:hi>Iewes</ns0:hi> were incensed against him; that Troubles did abide him, or wait for him in <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi> whither he was going, <ns0:hi>vid. Act.</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>0.23. And it hapened accordingly, for the <ns0:hi>Iewes</ns0:hi> went about to kill him, <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 21.31. Therefore tis, that he de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sires their <ns0:hi>Prayers, That he might be delivered from them, vid.</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Thes.</ns0:hi> 3.2. <ns0:hi>Secondly,</ns0:hi> That the Almes he brought the Poor <ns0:hi>Saints</ns0:hi> at <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> might be taken by them in good part: That they might be reconciled, both to the <ns0:hi>Gentile</ns0:hi> Churches that sent it, and to him that brought it. It detracts greatly from a <ns0:hi>Gift,</ns0:hi> when it comes, either from one, or by one; against whom we are prejudic'd.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32. <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 18.21.</ns0:note> That I may come unto you with joy <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Act. 18.21.</ns0:note> by the will of God <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> This would be a means to make me come unto you with the more comfort if God will, or if God grant it to our Prayers. This condition (if God will) he had before inserted upon this very occasion, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 1.10. See the like 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 4.19. <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> 4.13, 15. This he did to free himself from the suspition of inconstancy, in case it should fall out otherwise: as also to shew. That alwayes, and in all things he referred himself to the good Pleasure and Providence of God.</ns0:note>, and may with you be refresh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> With your Company and Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />verse. This hath the same sence with <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 1.12. See the Notes there.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33. Now the <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Cor. 14.33.</ns0:note> God of peace <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">This is a frequent Title of God in Scripture, he is called the God of Peace, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 16.20. 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 13.11. <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 4.9. 1 <ns0:hi>Thes.</ns0:hi> 5.23. 2 <ns0:hi>Thes.</ns0:hi> 3.16. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 13.20. Here it fits his great Argument, which was to perswade the Believing <ns0:hi>Romans</ns0:hi> to be at peace amongst themselves, and not to contend a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bout indifferent things.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> with you all <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">Three times in this Chapter doth the Apostle lift up a Prayer for the Believing <ns0:hi>Romans. vid. v.</ns0:hi> 5.13. And this is more comprehensive than the o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther two. If God be with us, no good thing can be want<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing to us. Gods presence is inclusive of all good, and ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />clusive of all evil.</ns0:note>. Amen <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>vid. chap.</ns0:hi> 16. <ns0:hi>ult.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
            </ns0:div>
